Section F · Design Principles

Principles that guide Meld

Five core tenets shaping every token, component, and interaction model in the system.

Principle 01

Consistency

Create predictable, intuitive experiences across products and platforms. Shared token semantics guarantee that behaviors and visuals feel cohesive everywhere.

Principle 02

Accessibility

Make experiences usable by people with diverse abilities. Every component is built with WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, keyboard navigation models, and ARIA landmarks by default.

Principle 03

Clarity

Prioritise understandable interfaces and meaningful interactions. Remove visual clutter, make interactive states unambiguous, and communicate system status instantly.

Principle 04

Flexibility

Support varying product domains from consumer applications to high-density enterprise data grids without compromising design integrity or system speed.

Principle 05

Scalability

Build enduring architectural foundations that evolve with growing products and teams. Modular token hierarchies and systematic workflows prevent fragmentation.

Get Started · Overview & Quick Start

Getting Started with Meld

Meld is structured to be adopted incrementally. Whether you are using raw design tokens, copy-pasting HTML/CSS primitives, or consuming Figma assets, here is how to get up and running in minutes.

System NameMeld by IDEOCurrent Versionv1.2.0 (Actively Maintained)
TypefaceSpace GroteskLicenseMIT Open Source
Figma LibraryAvailable in Figma CommunityGitHub Repomeld-design-system

1. Quick Start with Design Tokens

All Meld components and themes are powered by semantic CSS custom properties. Import Space Grotesk and link the Meld stylesheet in your document head:

<!-- 1. Space Grotesk Typeface -->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Space+Grotesk:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

<!-- 2. Meld Tokens & Primitives -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/akshayashokanpothan/meld-design-system@main/index.html">

2. Theme Setup

Meld features full dual-theme support. Toggle themes simply by setting the data-theme attribute on the <html> root element:

// Toggle theme programmatically
const isDark = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark';
document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', isDark ? 'light' : 'dark');

3. Designer & Developer Workflows

Designer Workflow

1. Duplicate the Meld Figma Library.

2. Publish as an organization or team library.

3. Use approved Space Grotesk text styles and OKLCH color styles.

4. Insert components and inspect component variants.

Open Figma Specs →

Developer Workflow

1. Reference semantic tokens rather than hardcoded hex values.

2. Follow WCAG 2.2 AA target size (minimum 40px touch targets).

3. Test responsive behavior across all 9 viewports (320px–1920px).

4. Track additions in changelog.json.

Open Component Explorer →
Home / Design Principles

Guidelines · Foundations of Experience

Design Principles

Our design principles establish clear criteria for evaluating decisions, balancing trade-offs, and maintaining high design craftsmanship across all IDEO digital touchpoints.

Principle 01

Consistency

Create predictable, intuitive experiences across products and platforms. Shared token semantics guarantee that behaviors and visuals feel cohesive everywhere. When users learn how a button, input, or table works in one product, that knowledge transfers immediately to all other Meld experiences.

How we apply itUnified tokens across CSS & Figma; standardised state lifecycles (Default, Hover, Active, Focus, Disabled).
Principle 02

Accessibility

Make experiences usable by people with diverse abilities. Every component is built with WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, keyboard navigation models, and ARIA landmarks by default. Accessibility is never treated as a post-launch audit; it is a core structural constraint from day one.

How we apply itMinimum 4.5:1 text contrast in both themes; 40px minimum touch targets on mobile; visible focus rings; Escape key dismissals.
Principle 03

Clarity

Prioritise understandable interfaces and meaningful interactions. Remove visual clutter, make interactive states unambiguous, and communicate system status instantly. High information density should never mean visual chaos.

How we apply itSpace Grotesk typography hierarchy with high legibility; explicit saving/saved feedback states; unambiguous destructive action dialogs.
Principle 04

Flexibility

Support varying product domains from lightweight consumer mobile apps to high-density enterprise data grids without compromising design integrity or system performance.

How we apply itDensity switchers (Compact, Default, Relaxed); modular slot architecture; multi-device fluid layout clamping.
Principle 05

Scalability

Build enduring architectural foundations that evolve with growing products and teams. Modular token hierarchies and systematic contribution workflows prevent fragmentation as new components and patterns emerge.

How we apply itSingle source of truth changelog.json; automated multi-viewport testing; strict component checklist criteria.

About Meld by IDEO

Meld is an open-source design system created to unify digital products, design exploration, and software engineering. It represents IDEO's belief that great design systems do not restrict creativity—they liberate teams to solve higher-order human problems.

Typography

IDEO Website Design System

This module establishes the rules for typeface selection, hierarchy, sizing, spacing, responsive behavior, and implementation. It is a proposed specification, not an official IDEO brand guideline.

    Section 02 — Typeface Foundations

    Space Grotesk

    Primary typeface for the entire website. Use 400, 500 and 600 for most interface typography; reserve 700 for selected emphasis.

    Fallback familyfont.family.fallback → Arial, sans-serif
    Supported weights300–700 via the Google Fonts variable file (wght@300..700). Light (300) is a foundation weight only; it has no primitive token.

    Color module · 08 — Accessibility and Contrast Checker
    Contrast checker
    

    Thresholds (WCAG 2.2 AA): normal text 4.5:1; large text (18pt regular / 14pt bold) 3:1; meaningful UI components and graphics 3:1. Passing one does not imply passing the others. This tool validates chosen pairs only; it does not certify the website as WCAG compliant. Brand hex values are never changed automatically.
    

    

    

    

    

    Required test combinations (calculated)
    

    • Color must not be the only means of communicating information.
    • Focus indicators must stay visible against every background.
    • Disabled elements should remain understandable (labels, not just faded color).
    • Links need sufficient contrast and a non-color cue such as an underline.
    • Brand identity does not override accessibility requirements.

    Color module · 11 — Figma Implementation Guide
    Figma variables
    

    1. Collection “Primitives” (one mode): groups brand, neutral, pink, indigo, success, warning, error, information. Create color variables such as brand/primary = #BC4989 and neutral/950 = #171717 using the values in Section 03.
      2. 

    2. Collection “Semantic” with modes Light and Dark: groups text, surface, action, border, icon. Every variable is an alias to a primitive, e.g. text/primary → Light: neutral/950, Dark: neutral/50 (see Section 04).
      3. 

    3. Collection “Components”: groups button, card, input, navigation, link, each aliasing a semantic variable (Section 07).
      4. 

    4. Apply Components or Semantic variables to fills and strokes of reusable components, then switch the frame’s variable mode to test Light and Dark.
    

    Figma variable collections are design-file constructs; CSS custom properties (Section 12) are the code equivalent. Creating variables does not by itself restyle existing components or configure the codebase: each fill and stroke must be bound to a variable.

    Color module · 13 — Usage Guidelines
    Usage guidelines
    

    Do
    • Preserve approved brand colors.
    • Use semantic tokens in components.
    • Balance expressive brand accents with neutrals.
    • Validate contrast for actual pairs.
    • Keep semantic meaning the same across themes.
    • Use feedback colors consistently.
    • Use color to establish hierarchy.
    • Test states against the real component background.
    

    Don’t
    • Hard-code random HEX values in components.
    • Use brand colors for every background.
    • Assume white text works on every light tint.
    • Use color alone for errors or success.
    • Change a brand color for one component without documenting it.
    • Reuse a raw color for unrelated purposes without an intentional alias.
    • Claim compliance without testing real components.

    Components module · 01 — Overview
    Components
    

    Proposed component specification for Meld by IDEO: 13 categories and the full requested inventory, each with priority metadata, anatomy, variants, sizes, states, properties, behavior, accessibility, token mapping, Figma recreation guidance and an acceptance checklist. Colors and typography come from the modules above; anything not defined there is marked Proposed.
    

    Honesty note. Specs are written at archetype level (for example “button-like action” or “date picker”) and then personalised per component with its name, category, priority and neighbours. Treat component-specific details as review items. Previews are simulations in this page: nothing is uploaded, paid for, authenticated or sent to a backend.
    

    

    Categories and priority
    

    P0 Core · P1 Extended · P2 Specialised (conditional, build when a real use case exists). Priority never removes a component from the inventory.
    

    Shared state model
    

    States used: Default/Rest, Hover, Focus-visible, Pressed/Active, Selected, Disabled, Loading, Invalid/Error, Success, Read-only, Empty, Expanded/Collapsed, Checked/Unchecked/Indeterminate, Dragging/Drag-over, Visited, responsive behavior, Light and Dark. Each component documents only the meaningful subset.
    

    DistinctionRule
    

    Disabled vs read-onlyDisabled is not focusable or editable and is excluded from submission. Read-only stays focusable and readable, and is submitted but not editable.
    

    Selected vs pressedSelected is a persistent choice (tab, option). Pressed is the momentary active moment, or a toggle’s on state, exposed with aria-pressed.
    

    Invalid vs error feedbackInvalid is the field state (aria-invalid plus border). Error feedback is the message that explains and fixes it. Both are needed.
    

    Loading vs disabledLoading is temporary and busy (aria-busy) while content or context stays visible. Disabled is unavailable until something changes.
    

    Component vs application stateComponents own visual and interaction states. Application states (offline, quota reached, no permission) are passed in as props and shown with Feedback components.
    

    Valid combinationsExamples: loading button (non-interactive), invalid field that is also focused, checked and disabled checkbox, selected tab with keyboard focus, table loading while rows stay visible. Impossible combinations (loading + hover feedback) are not documented.

      Components module · 03 — Figma Recreation Guide
      Recreating the library in Figma
      

        

      1. Naming: Meld / Actions / Button, Meld / Forms / Text Field, Meld / Navigation / Tabs, Meld / Feedback / Alert, Meld / Website / Project Card. Variant properties read Variant = Primary, Size = Medium, State = Default.
        2. 

      2. Component set vs standalone: use a component set when a component has two or more variant properties (Variant × Size × State). Use a standalone component for single-form pieces (Divider, Code Block). Compose larger parts from nested instances, never from detached frames.
        3. 

      3. Properties, not variants: optional parts become Boolean properties (Leading icon), labels become Text properties, replaceable icons become Instance-swap properties. Do not multiply variants for what a Boolean can do.
        4. 

      4. Auto Layout: every component uses Auto Layout. Set direction, padding, gap and alignment per component (see each Figma panel). Prefer Hug for width unless the component has a Full-width property; wrap text with Fill container and a minimum width.
        5. 

      5. Variables: bind fills, strokes and text to the existing Semantic color collection (Light/Dark modes) and to the typography styles from the Typography module. Add the proposed variables (spacing, sizing, radius, focus ring, motion) in a new “Layout” collection; do not duplicate existing variables.
        6. 

      6. States: model Default, Hover, Focus-visible, Pressed and Disabled as the State variant property. Model Loading, Invalid and Selected as variants only when visuals differ. Add interactive-component prototypes for Hover, Pressed and open/closed overlays.
        7. 

      7. Review: switch the frame variable mode between Light and Dark for every component before ticking its checklist.
      

      Creating variables and components in Figma does not enforce accessibility or implementation; keyboard behavior, focus management and announcements are engineering verification items.

        Patterns module Â· 03 - Figma Recreation Guide
        Recreating UX patterns in Figma
        
  
        Patterns are not oversized monolithic master components. In Figma, patterns are system assemblies composed of existing Meld components, structured with Auto Layout and variable modes.
        
  
  
          
    
        1. Assembly over Monoliths: Assemble patterns from instances of canonical Meld components (Button, Text Field, Modal, Card, Badge). Do not detach components.
          2. 
    
        2. Figma Page Organization: Group patterns in Figma under Patterns / [Category] / [Pattern Name] (e.g. Patterns / AI / Human-in-the-Loop Approval).
          3. 
    
        3. Responsive Frame Sets: Document each pattern across three responsive breakpoints: Desktop (1280px / 1440px), Tablet (768px), and Mobile (375px / 390px) using Auto Layout with fill-container rules.
          4. 
    
        4. Dual Variable Modes: Bind every fill, stroke, and typography style to the Meld token collections. Toggle between Light and Dark mode on the parent frame to verify high contrast across all states.
          5. 
    
        5. Interactive Prototype Flows: Use Figma component interactions for state transitions (Hover, Pressed, Focused, Open/Closed) and create linked prototype flows for multi-step sequences (e.g. Onboarding Stepper, Human Approval Gate, AI Token Streaming).
          6. 
    
        6. Engineering Handoff Annotations: Explicitly annotate asynchronous behaviors that cannot be fully expressed in Figma prototypes: screen reader live region announcements (aria-live), focus restoration, API timeouts, and fallback error recovery.
          7.
